articles.body:
Candidatos ao governo da Bahia em 2026 — Foto: Reprodução/DivulgaCand

Os candidatos ao governo da Bahia cumpriram compromissos de campanha neste domingo (30). Entre as atividades do dia, estiveram carreatas, comícios e participação em protestos.

O candidato do União Brasil promoveu uma carreata pelas ruas do Subúrbio Ferroviário de Salvador , acompanhado pelos candidatos ao Senado Angelo Coronel (Republicanos) e João Roma (PL), o prefeito da capital, Bruno Reis (União Brasil), a vice-prefeita Ana Paula Matos e outros aliados.

O atual governador da Bahia passou o dia percorrendo o interior do estado. Ao lado de Rui Costa e Jaques Wagner, candidatos ao Senado, Jerônimo participou de caminhadas em Itatim e Milagres . Depois, fez carreata em Iaçu e, de lá, seguiu para um comício em Itaberaba .

O candidato da Unidade Popular recebeu a candidata a vice-presidente da República pelo partido. Pela manhã, eles seguiram em caminhada no bairro do Uruguai, em Salvador, junto a apoiadores. Depois, acompanharam o ato contra a escala de trabalho 6x1 no Farol da Barra. A última atividade do dia foi um ato de campanha em Simões Filho , na região metropolitana.

A candidata do Partido da Causa Operária fez panfletagem nas ruas, na cidade de Rio de Contas.

O candidato do Democracia Cristã participou de uma caminhada em Lauro de Freitas, na Região Metropolitana de Salvador (RMS), em apoio a um candidato a deputado estadual pela manhã. Mais tarde, percorreu as ruas do Pelourinho, na capital.

O candidato Ronaldo Mansur participou do ato contra a escala de trabalho 6x1, que reuniu artistas, militantes e apoiadores da causa na Barra, em Salvador. Na sequência, visitou o bairro Ilha de Maré.

articles.title: Kharge venue row: FIR against Rahul Gandhi for ‘giving caste angle’
articles.summary: FIR filed against Rahul Gandhi in Haldwani over remarks on Kharge rally venue “purification,” alleging hurt caste sentiments under BNS and SC/ST Act.
articles.body: DEHRADUN: In a fresh development in the controversy over an alleged purification ritual at the venue of a rally addressed by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge in Haldwani, Uttarakhand, a case was registered against Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi at Kotwali police station on Sunday night.The FIR — lodged under BNS sections 196 and 299, along with section 3(1)(q) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 — followed a complaint by Amit Kumar, a resident of Jawahar Nagar Colony in Haldwani and member of Shriram Sena Dharmarth Seva Samiti.Kumar, who belongs to the SC community, alleged that Gandhi gave a caste angle to routine cleaning work carried out at Ramlila Maidan on Aug 11, characterising the clean-up as an act of untouchability and a criminal offence during a news conference in Delhi.Kumar further alleged that caste sentiments were hurt by Gandhi’s statements. He asserted that Rahul Gandhi used “caste-indicative and insulting words against the Scheduled Caste” based on false and incomplete facts, thereby inciting hostility within the community.Nainital SSP T C Manjunath confirmed the development, saying, “Amit submitted all the required evidence to substantiate his allegations, following which an FIR has been registered. ASP Amit Saini will be heading the probe.”On August 8, Kharge addressed a public gathering at the Ramlila Maidan. Two days later, members of the right-wing group Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas Sangathan performed a havan for the shuddhikaran (purification) of the grounds.Members of the organisation stated that they conducted the ritual to counter slogans raised by Congress members during the rally, as well as a previous statement by Kharge in which he had “compared the BJP and RSS to a poisonous snake.”Kharge subsequently raised the issue in Rajya Sabha, demanding that cases be registered under laws prohibiting untouchability against those who “purified” the stage in Haldwani, and that the individuals involved be arrested and jailed.
